About Nine-ball

Nine-ball reuses the Pool table, ball sprites, pockets and impact sounds, with the rules swapped for nine-ball: nine object balls in a diamond rack, and the cue ball must contact the lowest numbered ball first.

A legal 9-ball wins the frame immediately, while a 9 on a foul loses. Play the computer when alone, or create a room and send the invite link to a friend.

How to play

  1. Nine balls are racked in a diamond with the 1 at the apex and the 9 in the centre; every shot must first contact the lowest ball.
  2. Potting any ball without a foul keeps the turn. Missing the lowest ball first or scratching is a foul and gives the opponent an extra shot.
  3. Legally potting the 9-ball wins at once; a 9-ball on a foul loses. The frame is capped at 200 shots.

Frequently asked questions

How is Nine-ball different from Pool?
Pool is grouped eight-ball: clear your group, then pot the 8. Nine-ball has no groups — hit the lowest ball first and pot the 9 to win.
Do I have to call pockets?
No. This is a simplified casual variant with no called pockets, push-out or three-consecutive-foul rules.
Can I invite a friend?
Yes. Create a room, share the invite link and you both land on the same table, taking alternating shots.
